translation.en: the winds, or their blessing (what Skyborne greetings and farewells invoke)
translation.uk: вітри або їхнє благословення (те, що закликають привітання і прощання небесонароджених)

notes: Darnassian (Skyborne dialect). In every elvish formula of the Skyborne voice files: banu alah and banu adora (greetings), aradash ... banu (a greeting) and aeesha'el banu zephrali (a farewell), and written once in the letter MailTemplate 652. It takes the place of Elune in Darnassian Elune-adore 'Elune be with you' and of ishnu 'good fortune' in Ishnu-alah 'good fortune to you', so it names what the blessing wishes on the listener. Nearly every English greeting and farewell of the same NPC voices invokes the winds ('Favorable winds to you, friend', 'Winds welcome you', 'Blessing of the winds upon you', 'May the winds guide your path'), and the letter that ends with it says 'I am unsure where the winds will lead you'. Whether banu is the winds themselves or their blessing is open. Replaces the low 'way, passage' guess of report 3.

The only Skyborne sentence in the client: the valediction of MailTemplate 652, from the Valanaar druid trainer Lotheluum Starbreeze to a young Skyborne druid ($n) after the Bear Form quests, in the slot where other letters close with 'Regards,' or 'Light be with you.' zepharaalis = Zephraalis, a Skyborne surname built on Zephras. aeesha'el and banu are attested nowhere else; their glosses are guesses. new: Darnassian (Skyborne dialect). The only written Skyborne sentence in the client: the valediction of MailTemplate 652, from the Valanaar druid trainer Lotheluum Starbreeze to a young Skyborne druid ($n) after the Bear Form quests, in the slot where other letters close with 'Regards,' or 'Light be with you.' zepharaalis = Zephraalis, a Skyborne surname built on Zephras. Skyborne NPCs speak the same farewell with zephrali as the last word (aeesha'el banu zephrali, report 5), and banu also opens their greetings banu alah and banu adora, so banu is what the blessing invokes (the winds, or their blessing); aeesha'el is still unexplained.
